# Headache-Reducing Wellness Snapshot

A simple non-prescription routine can often help lower headache frequency and improve sleep by targeting the most common triggers: inconsistent hydration, caffeine swings, poor sleep timing, and allergy irritation. Since you have mild seasonal allergies and no asthma, this plan leans on steady habits and low-risk comfort measures.

# 7-Day Headache + Sleep Reset Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg

| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Drink 16–20 oz water; get 10 minutes of outdoor light | Keep caffeine to your usual amount; no extra serving | Set a fixed bedtime; screens off 30 minutes before sleep |
| 2 | Water on waking; eat breakfast with protein | Short walk or stretch break; note any headache triggers | Cooler, darker bedroom; same bedtime |
| 3 | Repeat hydration; avoid skipping meals | If you use caffeine, take it before noon | Gentle wind-down: reading, shower, or breathing exercise |
| 4 | Morning light exposure; water first | Allergy control: shower after outdoor exposure; change clothes | Keep sleep schedule steady even if you feel tired earlier |
| 5 | Hydrate steadily through the day | Limit caffeine to one earlier dose only | Avoid alcohol close to bedtime; no late heavy meal |
| 6 | Same wake time; water + breakfast | Take a 5-minute posture break every 2–3 hours | Relaxation routine: slow breathing or body scan |
| 7 | Review the week: headache days, sleep quality, triggers | Repeat what helped most | Plan next week with the same wake/bed times |

## Hydration and Caffeine Guidance

- **Hydration target:** aim for about **2–3 liters of fluid per day** for many adults, adjusting for heat, exercise, and body size.
- **Simple rule:** drink a glass of water at waking, with each meal, and after exercise.
- **Headache prevention tip:** dehydration can trigger headaches, so try not to go long stretches without fluids.
- **Caffeine:** keep intake **consistent** day to day; sudden increases or skipped usual doses can trigger headaches.
- **Best timing:** have caffeine earlier in the day, ideally **before noon** or at least **8 hours before bedtime**.
- **Sleep impact:** if sleep is light or delayed, reduce caffeine gradually rather than abruptly.
- **Practical ceiling:** many adults do well staying at or below **400 mg/day** total caffeine, but a lower amount may be better if you’re sensitive.

## Red-Flag Symptoms That Need Medical Care

Seek urgent medical care if a headache is:

- **Sudden and severe**, especially if it peaks within seconds to minutes
- **The worst headache of your life**
- Accompanied by **fever, stiff neck, confusion, fainting, or seizure**
- With **weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, facial droop, or vision loss**
- After a **head injury**
- New and persistent with **vomiting**, especially if you can’t keep fluids down
- Associated with **chest pain, shortness of breath, or severe high blood pressure symptoms**
- **New or clearly worsening** over time, especially if headaches are becoming more frequent
- Different from your usual pattern, or triggered by **coughing, exercise, or sex**
- Occurring with **pregnancy** or postpartum, if relevant

## Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: Track headaches] https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/headaches/
- Action: [Button: Sleep hygiene tips] https://www.cdc.gov/sleep/about_sleep/sleep_hygiene.html
- Action: [Button: Migraine warning signs] https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/migraine-headache/symptoms-causes/syc-20360201

## Sources

- NHS headache overview: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/headaches/

- Mayo Clinic migraine symptoms and when to seek help: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/migraine-headache/symptoms-causes/syc-20360201
